raw_response:
I have been farming these 200 mu for four years now. I am 48, finished middle school, and learned this business by watching my neighbors in Quzhou County and copying what works. I do not trust fancy advice from outsiders unless I saw it work in someone else's field first. With 200 mu, I have to think about my total budget — every bag of fertilizer is real money, but a bad harvest is worse than wasting a little input. I would rather apply a bit too much than risk losing yield.

My main system is wheat-maize on 120 mu. Last October I planted an improved wheat variety, Liangxing 77, same as my neighbor across the road. For that wheat, I put down one 50-kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu as basal, and I will top-dress twice with urea — once at green-up and again at jointing. That comes to about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu, 8 kg of phosphorus, and 5 kg of potassium. I will irrigate four times: winter water, green-up, jointing, and grain filling. I spray twice for insects and disease. I till with the rotary tiller before planting. Last year I got about 1,100 jin per mu; this year I expect 580 kg per mu if the weather holds.

After wheat harvest in June, I will plant hybrid maize — Nongda 372 or NK815, whichever the seed dealer has at a good price. I use no-tillage planting, seeding directly into the wheat stubble to save time and fuel. I apply 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, then side-dress with urea when the plants are knee-high. That is 16 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate three times in summer — the rain usually helps, so three is enough. Two pesticide sprays. I expect 650 kg per mu.

I grow cabbage on 40 mu. I use hybrid F1 seed, Zhonggan 56. Cabbage is a heavy feeder, so I apply two 50-kg bags of compound fertilizer per mu, split between basal and side-dressing. That is 20 kg nitrogen, 9 kg phosphorus, and 10 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate five times because cabbage heads will crack if the water is uneven. I spray three times for cabbage worms and mildew. I rotary till the land fine before transplanting. I expect 4,500 kg per mu.

Stevia is on the remaining 40 mu. I started it two years ago because the dealer said the price per jin is much better than grain. It is an improved variety. I apply one and a half bags of compound fertilizer per mu, about 15 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium. I irrigate four times and spray three times for pests. I rotary till before planting. Yield is smaller — about 500 jin per mu fresh leaves, so 250 kg per mu — but the money is good.

I worry about costs. Fertilizer is expensive this year. But I will not cut back. Last year I spent heavily and the yields paid off. My neighbor who tried to save money on urea lost two dan per mu on his wheat. I will do what I did last year, and maybe add a little extra on the wheat top-dressing to be safe.
